tagline: Repositioning an icon of the stage as a powerhouse of the studio: the visual launch of Fender Studio Pro and the Quantum LT interfaces.

p: Fender is a name built on the stage. Fender Studio Pro, the rebranded PreSonus Studio One Pro, and the new Quantum LT interfaces move that name into professional audio production. The brief was simple and hard: prove Fender belongs in the control room as much as under the spotlight.

Production spanned five shoots across three cities: the NYC hero film, three Nashville shoots for product demo, the Quantum LT launch and brand collateral, and a New Orleans shoot for the Fender Studio app that folded an earlier launch into the same family. Casting leaned young for a vintage-meets-modern aesthetic. The mission: hold the existing PreSonus demographic while drawing in a younger, more diverse crowd, the next generation of producers who find sanctuary in their studio.

cards: Concept, production, and direction of the NYC hero film and the Quantum LT hardware film.
Gaffer and lighting design across shoots, lit to feel like the room, not an ad.
Campaign and product photography, plus key art and YouTube thumbnails.
Mix engineering for the hardware film, including a remix of Nicole Alexis' original song for the cut.
Key art, thumbnails, social carousels, and campaign collateral.
Fender.com wireframing plus the Amazon storefront and A+ merchandising.

p: The hero film pairs Nile Rodgers with Alissia inside a working studio: proof that Fender Studio Pro is where real records get made. Shot at the legendary Power Station in Hell's Kitchen, NYC, a room Nile told us was built around Chic in the '70s. The keystone shoot of the whole campaign, and the one true hero film of the launch.

p: The films needed a home. I played a key role in wireframing and shaping the design, flow, and visual identity of the Fender Studio experience on Fender.com, defining how the ecosystem is introduced, navigated, and shopped.
Across 11 marketing landing pages: the Fender Studio brand page, the Fender Studio Pro launch page and its seven sub-pages, and the pages for Audio Interfaces, Notion, and Universal Control.

p: Film, photography, sound, web, and retail all speaking the same language. Fender's name carried convincingly from the stage into the control room, on brand and on time across every channel.
The launch met its internal targets across traffic, conversion, and revenue. Those figures are Fender's to share rather than mine, so this page stays on the creative.
